title: Cofibration local equivalences detected by strict mapping spaces
statement: Use the model, simplicial-model and derived mapping-space conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a left proper simplicial model category: pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence. Let $\mathcal Z$ be any class of fibrant objects closed under weak equivalences between fibrant objects. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$, write $f\in W_{\mathcal Z}$ if $\operatorname{Map}^h(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $Z\in\mathcal Z$. For every cofibration $i:A\to B$, with no cofibrancy assumption on $A$ or $B$, one has $i\in W_{\mathcal Z}$ if and only if $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(B,Z)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every $Z\in\mathcal Z$. A trivial Kan fibration means a map having the right lifting property against all boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$, as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Lemma A.3.7.1, printed pp. 906-908 (PDF pp. 923-925), with its proof: it uses only closure of the class of local fibrant test objects under weak equivalences. No Stacks tag supplies this mapping-space detection theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Choose a trivial fibration $f:A'\to A$ with $A'$ cofibrant, by factoring $\varnothing\to A$. Factor $if:A'\to B$ as a cofibration $i':A'\to B'$ followed by a trivial fibration $f':B'\to B$. Then $B'$ is cofibrant. Set $P=A\amalg_{A'}B'$, with maps $k:A\to P$, $g:B'\to P$ and $j:P\to B$ induced by $i$ and $f'$. Cofibrations are left lifting classes, so closure under composition and pushout gives that $k$ is a cofibration, as is $\varnothing\to B'$. Left properness applied to the pushout of $f$ along $i'$ says $g\in W$. Since $jg=f'\in W$, two-out-of-three gives $j\in W$, and $jk=i$. No cofibrancy of $A,B$ or $P$ has been asserted.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof, first diagram, printed pp. 906-907.

proof.text:
For any fibrant test object $T$, abbreviate the strict enriched mapping set by $M(X,T)$ and put $p_T:M(B,T)\to M(A,T)$, $r_T:M(B',T)\to M(A',T)$ and $q_T:M(P,T)\to M(A,T)$. The simplicial model axiom, applied to $i,i',k$ and $T\to1$, makes all three maps Kan fibrations. Because $A',B'$ are cofibrant, $M(A',T)$ and $M(B',T)$ are Kan complexes representing the corresponding derived mapping spaces. The square with vertical arrows $f,f'$ becomes a square of equivalences after localization. Consequently $i\in W_{\mathcal Z}$ if and only if $r_T$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $T\in\mathcal Z$. Tensoring with a simplex preserves the pushout defining $P$, since tensor is a left adjoint; the enriched tensor-Hom adjunction therefore gives, in each simplicial degree,
$$M(P,T)=M(A,T)\times_{M(A',T)}M(B',T).$$
Thus $q_T$ is the pullback of $r_T$ along $f^*:M(A,T)\to M(A',T)$.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof, printed p. 907, maps p, q and q-prime.

proof.text: For each vertex $t:A\to T$, precomposition with $j$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence between the strict fibers $(p_T)^{-1}(t)\to(q_T)^{-1}(t)$. Indeed, in the simplicial model category $\mathcal M_{A/}$, the objects $i:A\to B$ and $k:A\to P$ are cofibrant, the object $t:A\to T$ is fibrant, and $j:k\to i$ is a weak equivalence. The undercategory mapping formula identifies their enriched maps to $t$ with these two strict fibers. The derived-mapping comparison, applied in $\mathcal M_{A/}$, makes precomposition with this weak equivalence an equivalence of Kan complexes. The pullback in step 2 also identifies $(q_T)^{-1}(t)$ exactly with $(r_T)^{-1}(tf)$. This is a relative mapping argument, so it applies even when $A$ is not cofibrant and $M(A,T)$ is not Kan.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof, printed p. 907, comparison in the simplicial model category under A.

proof.text: We will also use the following relative fiber comparison. Let $c:A_0\to C$ be a cofibration, let $w:S\to S'$ be a weak equivalence between fibrant objects, and let $s:A_0\to S$ be a vertex of $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A_0,S)$. Then postcomposition with $w$ maps the strict fiber of $c^*:\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(C,S)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A_0,S)$ over $s$ to the strict fiber of $c^*:\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(C,S')\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A_0,S')$ over $ws$, and this map is a weak homotopy equivalence. Indeed, in the simplicial model category $\mathcal M_{A_0/}$ the object $c:A_0\to C$ is cofibrant because $c$ is a cofibration, the objects $s:A_0\to S$ and $ws:A_0\to S'$ are fibrant because $S,S'$ are fibrant, and $w:s\to ws$ is a morphism whose underlying arrow is a weak equivalence, hence a weak equivalence of $\mathcal M_{A_0/}$. The undercategory mapping formula identifies $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M_{A_0/}}(c,s)$ and $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M_{A_0/}}(c,ws)$ with the two strict fibers, and postcomposition with $w$ with the displayed map. For cofibrant source and fibrant targets, the derived-mapping comparison applied in $\mathcal M_{A_0/}$ represents $\operatorname{Map}(qc,qs)\to\operatorname{Map}(qc,q(ws))$ naturally in the localized target; since $qw$ is an equivalence, this map is an equivalence, so the strict map is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is the covariant counterpart of step 3. It needs no Kan hypothesis on $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A_0,S)$ and no comparison between ordinary fibers and homotopy fibers.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof, printed pp. 907-908, fiber comparisons; expanded as in step 3 through the simplicial model category under the source of the cofibration.

proof.text: Assume $i\in W_{\mathcal Z}$ and fix $T\in\mathcal Z$. Step 2 makes the Kan fibration $r_T$ a weak homotopy equivalence, hence a trivial Kan fibration by the fiber criterion. Pullback preserves the right lifting property against each boundary inclusion: a lifting square for the pullback is the same lifting square over the prescribed map to the base. Therefore $q_T$ is a trivial Kan fibration, and every vertex fiber of $q_T$ is contractible. Step 3 makes every vertex fiber of $p_T$ contractible as well. Since $p_T$ is a Kan fibration, the same criterion makes $p_T$ a trivial Kan fibration. This proves the forward implication, including the dimension-zero lifting condition.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof of (1) implies (2), printed p. 907.

proof.text: Now assume $p_T$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every $T\in\mathcal Z$. First consider a vertex of $M(A',T)$ of the form $tf$, where $t:A\to T$. The fiber $(p_T)^{-1}(t)$ is contractible by the fiber criterion. Step 3 and the exact fiber identification there imply that $(r_T)^{-1}(tf)$ is contractible. This argument holds for every $T$ in the entire class $\mathcal Z$, and not merely for the original test object that will be fixed next.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof of (2) implies (1), printed p. 907, vertices factoring through A.

proof.text: Fix $Z\in\mathcal Z$ and an arbitrary vertex $t':A'\to Z$. Factor it as $A'\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z$, with $u$ a cofibration and $v$ a trivial fibration. Since $Z$ is fibrant, so is $Y$ (right lifting classes are closed under composition, by successively lifting against the two factors). Thus $Y\in\mathcal Z$. Form $D=A\amalg_{A'}Y$. Left properness applies to the weak equivalence $f:A'\to A$ pushed out along the cofibration $u$, and gives a weak equivalence $Y\to D$. Choose a fibrant replacement $D\hookrightarrow V$ that is a trivial cofibration. Then $Y\to V$ is a weak equivalence between fibrant objects, so $V\in\mathcal Z$. The image of $u$ in $M(A',V)$ factors through $A\to D\to V$. Step 6 therefore says that the fiber of $r_V$ over that image is contractible. Closure of $\mathcal Z$ was used only for the fibrant objects $Y,V,Z$, never for the possibly nonfibrant pushout $D$.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, proof of (2) implies (1), printed pp. 907-908, replacement of the test object.

proof.text: Apply step 4 with $c=i':A'\to B'$, $A_0=A'$ and base vertex $u:A'\to Y$, first to the weak equivalence $Y\to V$ between fibrant objects and then to the weak equivalence $v:Y\to Z$ between fibrant objects. The first application identifies the fiber of $r_Y$ over $u$ with the fiber of $r_V$ over the image of $u$, up to weak homotopy equivalence. The second identifies the fiber of $r_Y$ over $u$ with the fiber of $r_Z$ over $vu=t'$. The fiber of $r_V$ over the image of $u$ is contractible by step 7. By two-out-of-three for weak homotopy equivalences to $\Delta^0$, the fiber of $r_Z$ over $t'$ is contractible. Since $t'$ was an arbitrary vertex, and $r_Z$ is a Kan fibration by step 2, the fiber criterion makes $r_Z$ a trivial Kan fibration, in particular a weak homotopy equivalence. This holds for every $Z\in\mathcal Z$; step 2 concludes $i\in W_{\mathcal Z}$ and proves the reverse implication.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.3.7.1, end of proof, printed p. 908; the comparison via Y and V retains the specified base vertices.

lean.statement: theorem cofibration_local_mapping_test {M : Type u} [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (cofibrations M) (trivialFibrations M)] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialCofibrations M) (fibrations M)] [SimplicialCategory M] (_T : SimplicialTensorCotensor M) (_hSM7 : SatisfiesSM7 M) (_leftProper : ∀ {A B C : M} (w : A ⟶ B) (i : A ⟶ C), WeakEquivalence w → Cofibration i → WeakEquivalence (pushout.inr w i)) (Q : M ⥤ M) (_ε : Q ⟶ 𝟭 M) (_hQ : ∀ X : M, IsCofibrant (Q.obj X) ∧ Fibration (_ε.app X) ∧ WeakEquivalence (_ε.app X)) (tests : ObjectProperty M) (_fibrant : ∀ Z : M, tests Z → IsFibrant Z) (_closed : ∀ {X Y : M} (w : X ⟶ Y), WeakEquivalence w → IsFibrant X → IsFibrant Y → (tests X ↔ tests Y)) {A B : M} (i : A ⟶ B) (_hi : Cofibration i) : (∀ Z : M, tests Z → SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (eHomWhiskerRight SSet (Q.map i) Z)) ↔ (∀ Z : M, tests Z → SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.I.rlp (eHomWhiskerRight SSet i Z))
lean.note: Derived precomposition is the actual enriched map induced by any functorial cofibrant replacement Q with trivial-fibration augmentation; the tests are already fibrant. No arbitrary mapping-space functor or comparison map is assumed. No cofibrancy is imposed on A or B.
